[WP] A child discovers a genie in a bottle..

During the first five hundred years of its imprisonment it had promised three wishes to its rescuer. Over the second five hundred years it had promised to destroy its rescuer.

The bottle opened suddenly. Tammie had been trying to find out what was inside the big metal bottle in the sand but it still surprised her when the stopper came out. She felt a good cry welling up. Then she realized that the bottle was open! And what had been inside the bottle came out! It was huge! At least a big as daddy! But nothing was a big as daddy. And this one was all sorts of funny colors. It was like one of those cloth things that mommy put her hand into and pretended to make speak. It was shouting something. It stomped around. That was silly. Tammie had tried stomping here but the sand just smushed out of the way instead of banging.

Bound by its promises it had to wait until the babbling girl child learned how to speak before she could speak her wishes. The freedom to do as it willed, promised when the seal on the bottle was broken, was cruelly denied. The genie ached in frustration and marveled again at the wickedness of mortals.

To the child, nothing was as terrifying as hunger.

Death, he had stared in the face countless times, and survived them all; but hunger!

There was no running away from the endless hunger that nipped at his heels, that gnawed at his stomach, that sapped at his strength and made gaunt his pale, sunken face.

He stumbled.

He fell.

Blank, soulless eyes stared accusingly at the uncaring sky above him.

Soundless curses drippped from his lolling mouth.

Then it happened - the sweet-grass voice that whispered softly in his ear.

Sweet voice as old as the earth itself, that whispered secrets in his ear...

Wordless, he got up. Unnatural strength flowed into his limbs.

Lethal LSD Lookalikes

Two years ago, police in Charleston, West Virginia, charged Todd Honaker with first-degree murder because his wife, Renee, died after consuming a drug he shared with her. Police and prosecutors identified the drug as LSD, which is what the Honakers apparently thought they were taking. That detail was puzzling, because no fatal LSD overdoses have ever been documented. As addiction specialist Paul M. Gahlinger notes in Illegal Drugs: A Compete Guide to Their History, Chemistry, Use and Abuse, "LSD is not toxic in the biological sense."

It turned out that the Honakers actually took 25B-NBOMe, a much newer psychedelic that is often sold on blotter paper and passed off as LSD. The novelty of the compound played a crucial role in the outcome of Todd Honaker's case, since the murder charge he originally faced, which carried a mandatory life sentence, can be used only in cases involving prohibited drugs. At the time of Renee Honaker's death, West Virginia had not yet banned 25B-NBOMe, which was discovered in 2004. Roane County Prosecuting Attorney Josh Downey therefore had to drop the murder charge. Honaker ultimately pleaded guilty to involuntary manslaughter and got a year in jail, nine months of which he had already served. Unlike LSD, 25B-NBOMe and a similar compound discovered in 2003, 25I-NBOMe, have been linked to several overdose deaths. It is hard to imagine a legal psychedelic market in which a well-studied, nontoxic substance is surreptitiously replaced by a novel, potentially lethal one.
